data.narrative:
Quobly is a seed-stage quantum computing company founded by Maud Vinet, Tristan Meunier, and François Perruchot. The quantum computing sector comprises 11 known comparable companies: 3 public (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private entities including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

Standard peer-median valuation methodology is not applicable here. The seed stage represents a structural gap within the quantum computing comp universe: zero same-stage peers, zero adjacent-stage peers, and zero similar-tier peers meeting minimum threshold requirements for reliable triangulation. The sector contains only 6 total quantum computing comparables, but none satisfy the narrow-filter criteria necessary to produce a defensible peer set of three or more datapoints. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material distortion given the extreme heterogeneity in stage, capital raised, and revenue generation across the broader quantum landscape.

This analysis cannot support a specific valuation range absent applicable quantitative methods and sufficient comparable data. The primary uncertainty is structural: quantum computing remains sufficiently nascent and dispersed across development stages that conventional comps-based valuation cannot be reliably executed. Any forward valuation of Quobly would require either (1) identification of additional seed-stage quantum peers with disclosed valuations, (2) use of alternative methodologies such as cost-to-build or scenario-based approaches, or (3) reliance on founder track record and technology assessments outside the scope of this comparative analysis.
